content: 1. Carefully adjust the dosage of antidepressants to achieve the desired therapeutic effect. This includes starting with the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose and monitoring the response, especially when co-administered with tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) and cobicistat. 2. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of doxepin cream by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Similarly, cobicistat also increases the levels or effects of doxepin cream through the same mechanism. Close monitoring is required. 3. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases doxorubicin levels or effects via the same pathway. Alternative therapies should be considered due to the potential for serious interactions. 4. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of liposomal doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect on liposomal doxorubicin. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases dronabinol levels or effects through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Dronabinol is a substrate of CYP3A4, and its levels can be significantly affected by strong inhibitors like cobicistat. Co-administration with cobicistat is contraindicated. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by mechanisms involving CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronedarone is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor/substrate and a CYP2D6 inhibitor. Co-administration with cobicistat is contraindicated. 8. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of drospirenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 10. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib exposure, raising the risk of toxicities. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 11. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Dose adjustments may be required, and alternative drugs should be considered. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz, in turn, decreases the levels or effects of darunavir and cobicistat, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors like cobicistat is contraindicated. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated, especially in poor or intermediate metabolizers. Dose adjustments are required for extensive metabolizers. 18. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to pharmacodynamic synergy and duplicate therapy risks. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 20. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase exposure to monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE). Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. Resume the previous dose of entrectinib after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 22. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, darunavir and cobicistat increase enzalutamide levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar but minor effect. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 25. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of ergonovine and ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated.
